clue.text: Variety of horsemeat in Sussex

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of horse are put into a new order

parts.note: ham is a cured meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: A local horsemeat product found somewhere in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'horsemeat' as one word, but the wordplay reads it as two: 'Variety of' works on the first half and the second half is a synonym. Sussex is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreham-by-Sea is a coastal town in the county of Sussex, so the definition names its location.

clue.text: Noises off in aspiration once for 9

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters of the word noises are rearranged

explanation.surface: Background noises interfering with someone's breathing, in a stage-direction sort of way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noises off' looks like the theatrical phrase for sounds from the wings, but 'off' is the anagram signal. 9 is CYPRUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Enosis was the movement for the union of Cyprus with Greece, a historical goal of Greek Cypriots.

clue.text: Not talking about right to have a meal with percussion

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for silent goes round the abbreviation for right

parts.note: dumb means silent, not talking
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A silent diner refusing to chat while a drummer bangs away at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumbeat is a stroke on a drum, the basic sound of a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Take away from French channel

parts.note: de is the French word for from
a duct is a channel or tube carrying liquid or air

explanation.surface: Subtracting something from a French waterway or TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct is to subtract, taking an amount away from a total.

clue.text: Cartesian premise making hit unhappily for writer?

indicators.note: unhappily means in a bad state, so the letters of hit are jumbled

parts.note: ink is what a writer writes with

explanation.surface: A philosopher's starting point turning a blow into something for an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Descartes, the Cartesian philosopher, began from 'cogito ergo sum'; the first two words in English are the answer. 'unhappily' rearranges HIT into ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes built his philosophy on the certainty of his own thinking, the premise of the famous cogito.

clue.text: Sceptical response is due with any morris dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests letters moving about, so due, any and morris are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that any morris dancing is owed, in a quaint English village scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks. 'is' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scornful retort meaning that what was said is only wishful thinking and will never happen.

clue.text: Day to finish with mate

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday, a day
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Going out with a mate at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is an informal synonym for a pal or companion.

clue.text: See 5
In stock at pharmacy but not really necessary?

definitions.meaning: able to be dispensed, available to be handed out by a chemist
capable of being done without, inessential

explanation.surface: A medicine available at the chemist that you could probably live without.
explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means able to be dispensed, and in ordinary use means something you can manage without.

clue.text: Ancient king keeping page in island

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the king's name contains the page

parts.note: Cyrus the Great was an ancient king of Persia

explanation.surface: An old monarch kept a young servant on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Feet? On conclusion of 5 across you can use transport …

parts.note: Descartes' cogito continues 'therefore' and ends with the two words for sum, giving IAM
buses are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: After finishing the philosophy, you can catch public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is unusual: Chambers allows it beside iambi.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambus is a metrical foot of one short then one long syllable, so the plural means poetic feet.

clue.text: … one of which takes 5 in maintained, wooded grassland

parts.note: refers back to the transport of the previous clue, so one of them is a single bus

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the Roman numeral goes into the word for kept

parts.note: held means maintained or kept up
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A bus carrying five people through wooded grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 10 across: 'which' means buses.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African term names open savanna country with scattered trees and scrub.

clue.text: When to eat and rise with Muppet Show

indicators.note: show suggests putting on a display, so rise and muppet are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Getting up and watching the Muppet Show at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muppet Show' looks like the TV title, but 'Show' is the anagram signal working on RISE plus MUPPET.
explanation.definitionFit: The hour of the evening meal is literally the time for the meal called supper.

clue.text: One wise group indigenous to 5 down 7, perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity
native means indigenous, belonging to a place by birth

explanation.surface: A wise band of natives belonging to a dreamy fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down 7 is the scornful phrase built at 5 down; something only imagined could be met with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful or invented thing belongs to the imagination, the kind of thing met with that scornful retort.

clue.text: Prize angle for those whose home is open to the public?

definitions.text: those whose home is open to the public?

parts.note: gold is a prize, a gold medal for first place
to fish is to angle

explanation.surface: A prize angler whose house is open to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A pet fish lives in a glass bowl, its life on view to everyone, hence the 'goldfish bowl' idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet fish kept in a clear glass bowl live where anyone can look in, a home permanently on public view.

clue.text: Boy or girl with tailless bird in test …

parts.note: Viv can be short for the boy's name Vivian or the girl's name Vivien

indicators.note: tailless means losing the end, so the last letter of the bird is dropped

parts.note: the avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill

explanation.surface: A child and a bird are being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the final T of AVOCET, leaving AVOCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an oral examination, a spoken test common in universities.

clue.text: … which infuses me with confidence

indicators.note: to infuse is to pour into, so the spoken word goes inside the letters of me

parts.note: refers back to the previous answer, a spoken exam, so it stands for oral

explanation.surface: Something that fills me with self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 15 down: 'which' stands for that answer's sense, spoken, ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Morale is a sense of confidence and good spirits in a person or group.

clue.text: Stairs in the air

definitions.meaning: a set of steps between floors of a building
the act of flying, travelling through the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a run of steps in a staircase and the action of flying through the air.

clue.text: Senior medico with prince and model

parts.note: con is the Italian and Spanish word for with
a sultan is a Muslim prince or ruler
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A top doctor arriving alongside royalty and a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a senior hospital doctor in Britain, a specialist above the junior grades.

clue.text: Weak king replacing island with island

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped for another, the king's letter standing in for island's

parts.note: Sicily is the island off the toe of Italy
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A feeble monarch swapping one island for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickly means in poor health and lacking strength.

clue.text: Yarn for a little without time and energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the small amount surrounds time and energy

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Some yarn for a small creature lacking time and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of 'outside', so the small amount wraps round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a fine strand of spun fibre, the same thing as yarn.

clue.text: See 11
Turn into the wind, in which I can turn back 5 down 7

indicators.note: in which says the second part sits inside the first
back means the sailing word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to luff is to steer a sailing ship towards the wind

indicators.note: turn means the letters of the words I can are reordered

explanation.surface: A sailor turning into the wind, believing they can turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: Two signals share the clue: 'back' turns the sailing verb round, and 'turn' rearranges the letters of 'I can', which sit inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only imagined is unrealistic, the kind of idea answered with that scornful phrase.

clue.text: Harry to wax enthusiastic about silver

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for enthusing goes round silver's symbol

parts.note: to rave is to talk enthusiastically
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Getting excited about a silver trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb meaning to raid or lay waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to attack and plunder, to lay waste, which is to devastate.

clue.text: Join up to harass most of nestlings

indicators.note: to harass is to disturb or agitate, so the letters are stirred up
most of means the word loses its last few letters, here three

explanation.surface: Signing up to pester young birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims nestlings to NESTLI, and 'to harass' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to join the armed forces, signing up for service.

clue.text: Bringer of luck for French gentleman at race meeting

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French gentleman
Royal Ascot is a famous English horse race meeting

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's lucky charm at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, whose June meeting is a society event.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object thought to bring good fortune.
